overview: Two blotting techniques from the same naming joke, detecting completely different types of molecules — RNA versus protein.
genZNote: Northern blot: 'is this gene being read?' Western blot: 'is the protein actually being made?'

aspects.label: Detection Method
aspects.valueB: Labelled antibody specific to the target protein.

aspects.label: Typical Use
aspects.valueA: Measuring gene expression at the transcript level.
aspects.valueB: Confirming presence, size, and relative amount of a specific protein; widely used in diagnostics like confirmatory HIV testing.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Western blot was historically the gold-standard confirmatory test for HIV, run after a positive ELISA screen.
overlay.memoryTrick: Northern = RNA. Western = protein (antibody-based, like 'W' for 'Which protein?').
overlay.commonMisconception: Western blot doesn't detect nucleic acids at all — mixing it up with Southern/Northern blot on exam day is a common and costly mistake.
